I farm this the way I usually do here: wheat first, then maize on the same 20.8 mu. I do not like gambling with yield. If I save a little on fertilizer and the crop turns weak, that loss is bigger than wasting one or two extra bags. I will still watch cost, because 20.8 mu is not small and every bag adds up, but with well water in hand I will push the field a bit rather than starve it. For wheat, I will use the kind most people around me plant now, not old seed kept too many years. I will put enough bottom fertilizer, plough after maize stubble if the land is hard, then give water at the key times. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like most neighbors do, because that is what gives grain if rain is uneven. After wheat harvest I will hurry the land, rotary till, sow fast, put fertilizer a little heavier at planting and then topdress once when the plants are growing strong. I will spray when I see real weed, worm, or disease pressure, not just for show. If the year is ordinary, I will count on decent wheat and decent maize, not the very highest yield people talk about on demonstration plots.
